chapter_theme: The lament turns from the breath to knowing: seeing within oneself instead of circling the world, passing from ignorance through grace-knowledge to the house of true knowledge, the fourth state, the light beyond the six adharas, the body of three malas seen as stainless, the three voids made void, 'you' seen in the sky-reality, the letters va, ma, si and a and their dying into the One, the Lord coming as guru, the 'I' that is really 'He', the magnet that draws iron to the feet, and the pranava cut through by holy madness.
structure_note: Loose runs: 101 to 107 on inner seeing and the ascent of knowledge; 108 to 110 on the body, the malas and karma; 111 to 114 on lights, dream and fullness; 115 to 118 on the voids and the letters; 119 to 125 on guru, self and the Lord, closing with the magnet and the pranava. The refrain எக்காலம் is constant and the reading is what each couplet adds.

101.reading: When will I run without running, go round the whole world, and without seeking behold it within myself?
101.nuance: ஓடாமல் ஓடி, running without running, makes the circuit of the world (வலம் வந்து, the pilgrim's circumambulation) an inner act, and தெரிசிப்பது (darshan) the sight that shrines promise is had என்னிடமாய், in oneself. The stanza completes 94's riding the breath instead of walking the earth.

102.reading: When will I leave ignorance, touch the limit of grace-knowledge, gain the house of true knowledge and come forth?
102.nuance: Three stages are named in order: அஞ்ஞானம், அருள் ஞானம், மெய்ஞ்ஞானம், with grace-knowledge as a stage that has a limit (எல்லை) to be touched and passed. மெய்ஞ்ஞான வீடு gives the work its title; வெளிப்படுவது is to emerge or be revealed, the poet's own coming out into the open.

103.reading: When will I watch until I win, leave all anger far behind, and direct my thought only as far as the word?
103.nuance: The two மட்டும் are the difficulty: வெல்லும் மட்டும் பார்த்து is 'watching until victory' (over anger, over the senses), and சொல்லும் மட்டும் சிந்தை செலுத்துவது may be 'sending the mind only as far as speech reaches', that is, no further than the guru's word, or 'letting thought go only so far as can be spoken'. The plain part is the leaving of anger.

104.reading: When will I seek the highest state, set the true reality within, seek the fourth state and gain it?
104.nuance: நாலாம் பதம், the fourth state, is turiya (beyond waking, dream and sleep) in the avastha scheme, or sayujya, the fourth and highest of the graded releases; மேலாம் பதம் may be the same thing or a step above it. The verse keeps the ascent in steps rather than naming the end.

105.reading: When will I see and know as light within a mirror, instead of counting and surveying, over and over, all the uncounted distances?
105.nuance: The contrast is between measuring what is far and seeing what is near: the image is at once in the mirror, as the light is, without the labour of range. The mirror is the mind or the inner eye in the tradition; the verse only gives the figure.

106.reading: When will I know myself, know the nature of being with my Lord, and be settled?
106.nuance: The order matters: self-knowledge first, then the knowledge of the Lord's company, then சமைந்திருப்பது, being composed or complete. எங்கோமான், our king, is the only name the Lord is given.

107.reading: When will I see the great light of bliss beyond the six adharas as my attainment, and possess it?
107.nuance: The six centres of the yogic body are passed, not dwelt in, and the light is above them. பேறு, attainment or gain, treats the light as a possession to be had rather than a place to be reached.

108.reading: When will I see and know, by seeing, free of pleasure, before the body perishes and goes through the delusion of anava?
108.nuance: ஆணவ மாயம் joins the first impurity (anava, the ego's darkness) to maya as the delusion that wears the body out. இன்பமற்று is odd: it may mean free of sense-pleasure, or be a corruption of இன்பம் உற்று (gaining joy), which would reverse it; and the repeated காணுதல் and கண்டறிவது make the sentence circular. The firm part is the deadline: before the body goes.

109.reading: When will I see this body, sprung up from the three malas joined together, as stainless, and be free of karma?
109.nuance: மும்மலம் is the Saiva triad anava, karma and maya; the body grows from them like a shoot (முளைத்தெழுந்த). நில்மலம் is நின்மலம், nirmala, stainless: the same impure body is to be seen as pure, which is the knower's body of the Tirumanthiram, not a different body.

110.reading: When will you be revealed and reached by me through the three kinds of seeing, so that former karma perishes?
110.nuance: மூன்று வகைக் காட்சி, the threefold seeing, is unexplained: the three means of knowledge (perception, inference, scripture), the three lights (sun, moon, fire, as at 148), or three eyes. முன்னை வினை, former karma, is what the seeing is to destroy.

111.reading: When will the light of the eye leaping, the grasping of the intent, and the seeing of the light of the sky all be revealed?
111.nuance: Three events are listed as past (பாய்ந்ததுவும், கொண்டதுவும், கண்டதுவும்) and their making-manifest is asked for: the poet has had the flashes and wants them to become open sight. In the yoga reading the eye-light is the brow centre and the sky-light the crown; plainly they are glimpses.

112.reading: When will I fix my thought in the supreme space, while you show me as in a dream and keep hiding?
112.nuance: காட்டி மறைத்து, showing and hiding, is the Lord's act of concealing (tirodhana, the Tirodhayi of 82); the poet's answer is not to wait for the showing but to hold the mind in the பரவெளி, the supreme space, steadily. The dream is the mode of the glimpse, not its content.

113.reading: When will I discern the one who asked 'who?', the knowledge that came and saw, and the one who said 'look'?
113.nuance: Three agents, three past acts: an asking, a seeing, a commanding. One reading makes them the soul (who asks), understanding (which sees) and the guru (who says 'see'); another makes all three the Lord's doing within. The verse asks only to tell them apart (பகுத்தறிவது).

114.reading: When will I see the full fullness, filling every thought I think, above the point, and shed pearls from my eyes?
114.nuance: முனை, the point, is read by the yoga tradition as the tip of the nose or the brow point where the gaze is fixed; above it is where the vision opens. முத்துதிர்ப்பது, pearls dropping, is tears of devotion; the fullness (பரிபூரணம்) is seen, not reasoned, and at 135 is what all inner speech is finally seen as.

115.reading: When will I love, with the three voids made void, the first void become emptiness, and that void too made void?
115.nuance: முப்பாழ் is Tirumular's three voids (of maya, of knowledge or space, of the soul in Siva-Shakti), and the verse voids them, voids the first void into சூனியம், and voids even that; what is left is அன்பு செய்வது, loving. Whether love is what is done in the last void or what remains when the voids are gone is not settled by the grammar.

116.reading: When will I see the sky-reality, that rose with 'see' and stood clear, as 'you', and gain a standing?
116.nuance: சீ யென்று எழுந்து is doubled: சீ is the letter si of சிவாய (so the reality rises with the mantra's letter, as 117 continues with va, ma and si), or a hiss or expulsion. நீ யென்று கண்டு, seeing it as 'you', rhymes the two syllables and echoes the great saying 'you are that'; the poet asks to see the vast reality as his own 'you', the second person, not yet as 'I'.

117.reading: When will I stand contained within the letter a, with the letter va and the letter ma become the sword, and the letter si?
117.nuance: The letters are those of சிவாயநம: va, ma and si are named, and அவ்வெழுத்து is the letter a (the first of Om, as the Kural's அகர முதல) or 'that letter'. The sword returns from 84: there the five letters together cut the mind, here two of them are the blade and the rest are sheathed in a. Tradition reads such letter-verses as the breath's syllables; the plain sense is the mantra folded into its first sound.

118.reading: When will I set my thought firmly in what stood as One when all the letters had died and perished, and take love?
118.nuance: After 117 has folded the letters into a, this voids even that: எழுத்தெல்லாம் மாண்டிறந்து, all letters dead, and the One (ஏகம்) standing without them. Love is again the last act, as at 115; the mantra is a ladder left behind.

119.reading: When will you take form as grace, being the beginning and the end, come as the guru, take me over and grant grace?
119.nuance: The guru is grace embodied (அருளாய் உருவாகி), and the one who is beginning and end comes in that form; ஆட்கொண்டு, taking as a servant, is the Saiva word for the Lord's claiming of a soul. The poet does not seek a teacher; he waits for the Lord to arrive as one.

120.reading: When will I know that all the time I did not know the one who knew as 'I', you were there as 'self'?
120.nuance: Three pronouns do the work: நான் (the knower who says 'I'), நீ (you, the Lord) and தான் (self, the third person). The claim is that the 'I' the poet never examined was all along 'you' standing as 'self'; knowing this is the whole request.

121.reading: When will I stand resting in what I have taken as His, after thinking over and over all that I had seen as mine?
121.nuance: என் மயம் and தன் மயம், 'of my nature' and 'of His nature', are the two ways of seeing the same things; the move is not to give things up but to re-see them as His. The thinking over (எண்ணி எண்ணிப் பார்த்த பின்பு) is the labour that precedes the rest.

122.reading: When will I know the way space is within space, as a form is born as light within light?
122.nuance: Two nested pairs, light in light and space in space, with the first given as the model for the second. The tradition reads the inner light born in the outer as the soul's light in the Lord's, and the space in space as the inner sky within the cosmic; the verse states only the nesting.

123.reading: When will I shut the true reality that gave light into the inner way, bring it out, seal it, and attain release?
123.nuance: அடைத்து, வெளியிட்டு, சாத்தி, shutting in, letting out and sealing, are the breath's words (the held breath, its release and the closing of the doors) in the yoga reading, applied to the மெய்ப்பொருள் held in the inner channel. Plainly it is a treasure locked away; the sequence of in, out and seal is what makes the breath reading natural.

124.reading: When will you leap, seize and draw me and set me at your feet, as a magnet pulls iron and draws it into its hand?
124.nuance: The magnet is the Lord and the iron the poet: the pull is the Lord's, and the poet asks only to be pulled. The same figure serves the Siddhars for the mind drawn to the Real and the Thiruppugazh for the man drawn to women.

125.reading: When will I take up madness, cut through the pranava, and wander like a red streak?
125.nuance: பித்தாயம் is unclear: பித்து (madness, the god-madness the Siddhars claim) with a suffix, or a corrupt word. பிரணவத்தை ஊடறுத்து, cutting through Om, is in the yoga reading passing beyond the sound to what is past it (the நாதாந்தம் of 149). செந்தாரை, a red stream or streak, is a meteor, a ray, or a flow of blood-red fire; the wandering is the freed madman's, taken up at 138.

links.note: Sivavakkiyar's crores ran and ran, sought and sought the light mingled within, withered and died; Pattirakiriyar asks to run without running and see without seeking, in himself. The same diagnosis, the light was inside, as a count of the dead in one and a request in the other.

Pattirakiriyar asks to seek and gain the fourth state; Tirumular says one who sees himself sees turiya, but if the turiya he contemplates is not made one with the Lord he is born again. If நாலாம் பதம் is turiya, the Tirumanthiram adds the condition the pulambal does not state.

Tirumular's unripe ones have a magic mirror risen in the mind yet never look at its reflection and go off desiring what is outside; Pattirakiriyar asks to see as light in a mirror instead of surveying the uncounted distances. Both set the mirror within against the search outside.

Tirumular praises the splendour that rises above the six-and-six supports; Pattirakiriyar asks to see the great light of bliss beyond the six adharas as his own gain. Both put the light above the centres rather than in the highest of them.

Tirumular says that for the knower the body itself becomes Siva and for the silent sage it is release; Pattirakiriyar asks to see the body grown from the three malas as stainless. The same body is re-seen, not replaced, in both.

82 asks the Tirodhayi, the concealing power, to show the way to grace; 112 describes the concealing in act, the Lord showing as in a dream and hiding again, and answers it not with a plea but with the resolve to hold the mind in the supreme space.

Tirumular names the three voids, of maya, of space and of the soul pervaded in Siva-Shakti, and ends speech in the pure form beyond them; Pattirakiriyar takes the three voids as given, voids them, voids the first into emptiness and voids that too, and ends in love. The pulambal pushes the Tirumanthiram's series one step further and names a different end.

Tirumular says the great saying 'you are that' ripens into 'I have become that' by Nandi's grace; Pattirakiriyar asks to see the clear sky-reality as 'you' and gain a standing. The pulambal stops at the first stage, seeing as 'you', which 120 then turns toward 'self'.

At 84 the five letters together are the sword that cuts the forest of the mind; at 117 two of the letters, va and ma, are the sword and the rest are contained in the letter a. The weapon is the same, and the second verse takes it apart letter by letter.

Tirumular says that when the two deeds balance, the sweet grace-power comes as the guru and removes qualities until one becomes Siva; Pattirakiriyar asks the Lord who is beginning and end to take form as grace, come as the guru and take him over. Both make the guru grace itself arriving in a form.

Tirumular says that once the flower called 'self' is laid at His feet, saying 'I' and 'He' is no longer right; Pattirakiriyar asks to know that the one he never knew as 'I' was all along 'you' standing as 'self'. Both dissolve the first person into the Lord, by offering in one and by recognition in the other.

The Kural cuts off the pride that says 'I' and 'mine'; Pattirakiriyar, after thinking over everything he saw as his own, rests in what he takes as His. The Kural removes the claim, the pulambal transfers it.

Pambatti tells the snake to join the mind to the visible Real as a magnet draws iron, and stay unshaken like a bucket and its rope; Pattirakiriyar asks the Lord to draw him to his feet as a magnet draws iron into its hand. The same pull, with the mind doing the joining in one and the Lord doing it in the other.

Arunagirinathar was drawn to women's breasts as a needle to a magnet and asks for the day grace fills him; Pattirakiriyar asks to be drawn like iron to a magnet to the Lord's feet. One magnet pulls down, the other up, and both poets ask for the same release from the pull.

source_issues: 108 line 2 இன்பமற்று may be a corruption of இன்பம் உற்று; the sense reverses with it.
125 line 1 பித்தாயம் is not a known word; பித்து with a suffix, or a corruption.
